prompt: Nowadays, many people drive to work or school instead of walking, cycling or using public transport. Does this trend have more advantages or more disadvantages?
essay:
An increasing number of workers are commuting by car rather than using more environmentally friendly methods of transportation. Although driving offers comfort and speed, I believe its environmental damage and the health problems of over-reliance on this approach may overshadow its advantages.

On the one hand, commuting to work by car is more comfortable than using other forms of transportation. Since this method does not require much physical effort, all people have to do is get into their vehicles, which are often parked outside their homes, and drive to their workplace. Furthermore, it can be faster than other methods, including buses and trains, which require people to walk to a station and may be affected by delays. For instance, during heatwaves in London, severe delays on the Underground can result in people who use the metro arriving late to work, while others who drive personal cars remain unaffected.

On the other hand, driving contributes to environmental deterioration because most cars burn petrol, releasing emissions that pollute the air and contribute to global warming. In contrast, walking and cycling produce no emissions, while public transport reduces pollution by carrying many passengers in one vehicle. Moreover, relying heavily on cars can cause health problems, particularly for office workers who spend long hours sitting and do little exercise. This lack of physical activity can increase the risk of obesity, diabetes and heart disease. For example, many office workers who rely on cars for commuting suffer from chronic conditions such as obesity and lower back pain. Therefore, I think that the drawbacks of this methods outwiegh the benefits by far.

To conclude, even though commuting to work by  car is more comfortable and convenient, the harm it does to the planet and  people's health is not worthwhile.
